stories.title: The Portlanders Turning Rescued Food Into Restaurant-Quality Meals
stories.label: people
stories.summary: In Portland, Oregon, a group called Urban Gleaners collects good food that would otherwise be thrown away. Chef Bradley Cohen and his team turn it into real, restaurant-quality meals. On a typical morning he might open the walk-in fridge to a pan of pork loins and a crate of fresh kale and zucchini, and invent a menu on the spot. The food reaches neighbors who need a good meal, and it stays out of the trash.
stories.why_good: A working local programme that cuts food waste and feeds people well, with dignity and care.

stories.title: Making Peace With a Himalayan 'Ghost'
stories.label: animals
stories.summary: In the high desert of Ladakh in the Indian Himalayas, villagers like Deachen Chuskit share their winter grazing lands with the elusive snow leopard. When snow covers the nearby pastures, herders have to take their livestock farther from home, which can put animals and big cats in each other's way. This story looks at how local people and conservationists are working to live alongside the 'ghost of the mountains' rather than against it. It is a hopeful look at communities and wildlife finding a way to share the same mountains.
stories.why_good: It shows people and one of the world's most elusive big cats finding a way to coexist, a conservation approach that is already under way in the communities it describes.
